I'm an old man, 70 now, but my body is still strong enough. My wife and I work this 30 mu together — our son works in the city, sends money back but doesn't come to the field. I use the village machine team for plowing, sowing, and harvest. I handle fertilizer and water myself.

**Winter wheat (planted last October, I'm thinking about spring management now, but this is my plan for the cycle):**
I plant Jimai 22 — same as Old Wang next door, he gets 450-500 jin per mu reliably. Seed 15 kg per mu, a little thick because our autumn was dry. Before sowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind, that's 50 kg. At greening in early March I topdress 25 kg of urea per mu along with the first irrigation. I water three times total — green-up, jointing, and heading. If the sky gives rain I skip one, but usually I water three. Spray once for aphids at heading, once for rust or scab if it's wet that year. Last year I got 460 kg per mu, this year I want the same.

**Summer maize (after wheat, June planting):**
I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever Xianyu the dealer pushes that year — everyone around me plants hybrids, no one uses old seed anymore. I don't plow after wheat — the machine drills the maize right into the stubble, saves money and keeps moisture. One bag of compound 15-15-15 (40 kg) goes in the row at sowing, then at big-trumpet stage in late July I put 30 kg urea per mu. Maize is hungry for nitrogen, I've learned that over the years. Usually one irrigation if July is dry, sometimes two. Spray once for corn borer, once more if armyworm shows up. I get about 550 kg per mu most years.

I don't like wasting fertilizer, but I'd rather put a little extra than watch the crop turn yellow. A bag of urea is 100 yuan — losing 50 kg of grain is 150 yuan. The math tells you what to do.
